newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Frogmen, helicopter join Colombia bus crash rescue.
newsitem.headline: Frogmen, helicopter join Colombia bus crash rescue.

text.p: Frogmen and an army helicopter were brought in on Sunday to help recover the remaining corpses from the wreckage of a bus that plunged down a deep ravine in the Colombian Andes.
The bus careered into the 1,500 foot (500-metre) deep canyon near the town of Ricaurte in southwest Narino province on Friday morning as the driver swerved to avoid a rockfall.
Red Cross officials said 37 people died -- most of them members of a single extended family -- while just three, including a 9-month-old baby, survived.
Heavy rain, thick fog and the steep-sides of the chasm have hampered rescue work and volunteers have taken two hours to bring a corpse up the ravine, Red Cross officials said.
Plans to use the helicopter to winch the remains of the bus out of a river at the bottom of the chasm were abandoned after rescuers decided the aircraft could not fly low enough.
Fire department divers searched for bodies in the canyon river, which has been swollen by torrential rain.
"Conditions are extreme. The weather has got worse with rain and heavy fog. That has slowed the work," said Mauricio Diaz, a Red Cross official in Narino.
"We still have to recover between 11 and 15 bodies from the canyon," he added.
